P_s3.explanation: The unit responds to small, round, dark, eye-like spots set in a lighter surround. Its main trigger is the eyes and snout of dog and fox faces, and it extends more weakly to eye-like objects such as blueberries, dashboard knobs, screws, remote-control buttons, a soccer ball and a toy's eye.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to small, round, dark, eye-like spots set in a lighter surround. Its main trigger is the eyes and snout of dog and fox faces, and it extends more weakly to eye-like objects such as blueberries, dashboard knobs, screws, remote-control buttons, a soccer ball and a toy's eye.
parsed.evidence: Animal faces make up about half of the top 20, with the boxes centered on the eyes or nose. The rest are compact round dark blobs such as blueberries (#1), knobs (#9, #11, #17), a screw (#15) and buttons (#14). The unit loses more than most units under luminance-polarity inversion (17th percentile) but survives patch shuffling and edge maps well, which fits a local dark-blob detector rather than a whole-face detector.
parsed.missing_data: Activation on isolated dark circular blobs versus cropped animal eyes and noses, to tell whether it is an eye detector that generalizes or a plain blob detector that dog faces happen to drive well.

P_s2.explanation: The unit detects small, dark, round, eye-like spots set in a lighter surround. Its main and most consistent case is the eyes and nose of dogs and other canids (wolf, fox, husky, beagle, corgi), and it extends more weakly to eye-like round objects such as blueberries, dashboard knobs and buttons, remote-control buttons, screw heads and a soccer ball.

parsed.explanation: The unit detects small, dark, round, eye-like spots set in a lighter surround. Its main and most consistent case is the eyes and nose of dogs and other canids (wolf, fox, husky, beagle, corgi), and it extends more weakly to eye-like round objects such as blueberries, dashboard knobs and buttons, remote-control buttons, screw heads and a soccer ball.
parsed.evidence: Twelve of the top 20 boxes sit on canid eyes or snouts, and the rest fall on small dark circular things (berries, knobs, bolts, buttons); random photos without these spots stay at 3-5. The unit loses more than most of its layer under luminance polarity inversion (percentile 17), which fits dark-on-light spots, and it holds up well under patch shuffling (percentile 89), which fits a small local feature rather than whole-object layout.
parsed.missing_data: Activation on synthetic dark dots versus light dots, and on dog faces with the eyes masked, would show whether the unit is a generic dark-blob detector or truly prefers eyes.

parsed.explanation: The unit detects a small, dark, roughly circular spot surrounded by lighter surround, a local 'dark round blob' detector. This fires on dog and fox eyes and noses as well as on blueberries, knobs, buttons, and indicator lights.
